title: Rust Worker 終於能從 panic 站起來——wasm-bindgen 接上 WebAssembly Exception Handling
summary: Cloudflare 在 wasm-bindgen 接上 WebAssembly Exception Handling proposal——Rust Workers 0.8.0+ 開 --panic-unwind、std 重 build 走 unwind、Walrus 解析 try/catch、出口走 extern "C-unwind"，panic 改以 PanicError reject 對應的 Promise。Durable Object 第一次能在單請求 panic 下保住 in-memory state。四層必須對齊：Rust compiler、wasm-bindgen tooling、EH proposal phase 4、Workers runtime。
widget_questions: Which layer in the four-layer stack (Rust compiler, wasm-bindgen tooling, WebAssembly EH proposal, Workers runtime) owns each piece of the panic-to-promise-rejection chain, and what does each one NOT know about the others?

What does a single Rust panic look like at each boundary before vs. after the EH proposal — source code that stays the same, wasm bytecode that flips from unreachable trap to try/catch/throw, and JS catch-path behaviour that changes from instance poisoning to a recoverable PanicError?

Which runtimes actually support the WebAssembly Exception Handling proposal today, in which versions, since when, and what does Cloudflare have to backport to keep Workers production on Node.js 22/24 LTS?

Which combination of the three required ingredients (panic=unwind compiler, wasm-bindgen with Walrus + extern "C-unwind", runtime with Exception.Tag support) is sufficient to produce a recoverable PanicError, and what failure mode kicks in when any one of them is missing?
